In practice it works like this: you register free, fund US$200, choose automatic or manual mode, and let the models propose entries across 9 assets while the practice account lets you learn without risk.
We reviewed the public record: pricing, restrictions, support hours, payout wording and every claim in between. Where the record contradicts itself, the scorecard marks it down.
whatItClaims: No platform fees - broker spreads and overnight charges still apply.
Payouts reportedly within a day.
9 crypto assets through broker partners.
A free demo account with practice funds.
Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
whatWeChecked: The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.
The performance story: no verified track record behind the return claims.
The number reuse: one score figure doing more than one job.
The deposit terms: minimum amount, payment methods and where the money sits.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: Can I trade manually?
faqs.a: Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$200 minimum.

faqs.q: What is the minimum deposit?
faqs.a: US$200, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

bottomLine: For a cautious newcomer, Randivura can work: start on the demo, deposit the US$200 minimum and keep your own numbers.
We scored Randivura 4.8 out of 5. The deductions come from the disclosure gaps, not the mechanics. With the US$200 minimum and the demo as guardrails, the risk stays yours to control.
